findings.issue: The spec's expectation framing — «Первый сигнал пользователь получает раньше — из verbose-панели [010]» plus the «Две подачи одного сигнала» constraint — rests on a panel field that is **superuser-only**. Verified live in the project's own image (lesovsky/pgcenter-testing:0.0.11, PG 14 and PG 18): `pg_ls_dir` has proacl `{postgres=X/postgres}` — no pg_monitor grant — while `pg_ls_waldir` and `pg_ls_archive_statusdir` both carry `{postgres=X/postgres,pg_monitor=X/postgres}`. The [010] backlog aggregate uses `pg_ls_dir('pg_wal/archive_status')` (internal/query/overview.go:100-102) and degrades that one field to `n/a` on 42501, so for a plain `pg_monitor` role — the canonical monitoring role, and the exact role the spec's privilege section is written around — the archiving backlog is simply absent from the panel. The new `archiver` screen, using the pg_monitor-granted `pg_ls_archive_statusdir()`, is the *only* place such a role ever sees the backlog.
findings.why_matters: Two consequences. (1) The 'this is a screen for analysis, not for detection' framing — the paragraph that limits what this feature promises — is factually wrong for pg_monitor roles: for them there is no earlier signal at all, and the screen *is* the detector. (2) A one-line swap inside the same area (`count(*) FILTER (WHERE name LIKE '%.ready') FROM pg_ls_archive_statusdir()` in place of the `pg_ls_dir` form, keeping the `× wal_segment_size` shape and the degrade-to-`n/a` wrapper) would give the panel the same audience as the new screen. The roadmap's mandate for [017] is precisely 'touch the WAL area once' — this is the moment when that swap is free, and after this feature it becomes a separate trip into the same code. Note the trade-off honestly: `pg_ls_dir` returns names only, `pg_ls_archive_statusdir` lstat()s every entry, so swapping makes the double directory walk the spec already documents in `Ограничения` into two lstat walks instead of one lstat + one readdir.
findings.fix: Take the decision explicitly in the spec rather than leaving it implicit. Either (a) add the [010] swap to scope in one sentence, and record in `Ограничения` that the doubled walk becomes twice as expensive on the verbose path (which also raises the value of the planned stand measurement — measure the verbose tick too); or (b) keep [010] as it is and correct the framing: state that the 'first signal in [010]' path exists only for superusers, and that for a `pg_monitor` role the `archiver` screen is the first and only place the backlog appears. Do not leave the current wording, which asserts a detection path most monitoring roles do not have.

findings.issue: The compatibility claim and its AC are scoped to «архив, записанный до 0.12 (PG 18 и старше)», but nothing says what happens to the case that falls outside that scope: an archive recorded by pgcenter 0.11 **against PG 19 beta**. Replay derives the layout from the recorded PG version, not from the recording tool version (`report/report.go:280-296`), so such an archive (7 recorded `wal` columns, `stats_age` at index 6) is replayed against the new PG 19 layout whose diff range is {2,6}. `diff()` (internal/stat/postgres.go:629-641) then feeds `stats_age`'s value (e.g. `12 days 04:11:56`) to `diffPair` → `strconv.ParseInt` fails → the report aborts with `diff failed: …` instead of printing.
findings.why_matters: It is a hard failure of `report -W w` with an error that names nothing the user can act on, and the affected population is exactly the people already running PG 19 beta with pgcenter — the project's own stands included. It is also a pre-existing property of the record format (any version-aware layout change has this exposure), so the right outcome is probably 'accept and say so', not new code — but that has to be written down, otherwise the golden tests (which will be generated from 0.12-recorded archives) certify a claim narrower than the one the spec makes.
findings.fix: Add one `Граничные случаи` bullet: an archive recorded by an older pgcenter *on PG 19* replays against the new 8-column layout and fails on the diff, because the layout follows the recorded PostgreSQL version rather than the recording tool version; state whether that is accepted (recommended — it is the format's pre-existing behaviour) and mention it in the 0.12.0 release notes alongside the `-W` change.

findings.issue: The feature adds a user-visible column (`fpi,KiB` on the PG 19 `wal` screen) but nothing in the spec covers its description text. `report -d -W a` is specified and has an AC; `report -d -W w` is not mentioned at all, and `report/describe.go:141` (`pgStatWALDescription`) has no row for the new column. `Критерии приёмки` line about docs covers only README (the `-W` flag) and the built-in help screen.
findings.why_matters: The describe output is the built-in documentation surface for a report's columns — the only place a user finds out what `fpi,KiB` means. A new column that appears in the table and not in `-d` is a half-shipped column, and this file is already version-approximate, so the omission will not be noticed later.
findings.fix: Add the describe text for the new `wal` column to the scope (one row in the existing description table) and an AC line for `pgcenter report -d -W w` on a PG 19 archive, matching the `-d -W a` AC that already exists.

findings.issue: The stand measurement in `Пользователь проверяет` — the mitigation that turns the accepted no-throttle decision into a known quantity — is not executable as written in two respects. (1) Leg (2), «для сравнения — время `pg_ls_waldir()` на соответствующем по размеру `pg_wal`», implies a `pg_wal` holding ~200 000 segments, i.e. ~3.2 TiB at the default 16 MiB segment size; no test stand carries that. (2) The `.ready` backlog is only stable while nothing is draining it: with `archive_command='/bin/true'` the archiver renames the 200 000 files away during the measurement, so the number being timed changes under the query.
findings.why_matters: This is the measurement that decides whether throttling comes back. A leg that cannot be run, and a backlog that evaporates mid-run, produce either no number or a number nobody can reproduce — which leaves the accepted risk in the same unobserved state the previous round flagged.
findings.fix: Two sentences in the same bullet: run the measurement with the backlog held still (`archive_mode=off`, or `archive_command='/bin/false'` so the archiver stalls on the first file), and state that the `pg_ls_waldir()` comparison is done on a synthetic `pg_wal` populated with the same number of zero-byte entries (only the per-entry lstat cost is being compared, not real segments) — or drop leg (2) and keep legs (1) and (3), which carry the decision on their own.

findings.issue: Carried over from round 1 and only partly addressed. The three deliverables (archiver screen + `w`/`W`; breaking `-W` with record/report; PG 19 FPI column + the two new `wal` replay goldens) are still not stated as independently deliverable, and the PG 19 half — the one hanging off a beta2 catalog — still has no stated fallback. The `Риски` entry says the name will be re-verified at RC/GA but not what happens then; the AC «на PG 19 экран `wal` содержит колонку `fpi,KiB`» becomes unsatisfiable if the column is renamed or dropped before GA, and the two new goldens would need regenerating. The stand-TTL risk («проверять экран `archiver` сразу, не дожидаясь record/report и FPI») implies the ordering but never says the parts can ship apart.
findings.why_matters: size M is defensible and the one-pass mandate is a good reason to keep the three together — no scope change is wanted here. But the FPI half is the piece most likely to move late, and without a written fallback the RC/GA re-verification has no defined outcome other than 'fix it', which is what turns a beta dependency into schedule risk for the two parts that do not depend on PG 19 at all.
findings.fix: One sentence in `Риски` or `Технические решения`: the three parts are independently deliverable in the order archiver screen → `-W` / record+report → PG 19 FPI column; if `wal_fpi_bytes` is renamed before GA the PG 19 branch and the goldens are regenerated, if it disappears the PG 19 branch is dropped and `wal` stays at the PG 18 layout — neither outcome touches the `archiver` screen or the `-W` change.

summary: Round-1's blocking finding and the three majors are genuinely closed — the cost of the unthrottled listing is now stated for TUI, record and the verbose double-walk, the privilege degradation is closed by live measurement rather than argument, the `-W` failure modes are split correctly, and the testing section is back at behaviour level; nothing in the current spec is unbuildable or mis-sized. One major remains: the spec's 'the first signal comes from the [010] panel' framing is contradicted by the ACLs — `pg_ls_dir` is superuser-only (verified live on PG 14 and PG 18), so a `pg_monitor` role never sees the panel's backlog and this new screen is its only source; either swap that aggregate to the pg_monitor-granted function while the WAL area is open, or correct the framing.
